title: Choose the visual world
question: 16 extreme-modern worlds for the marketplace. The roll assigned Factory Floor; all 16 are on the table. Pick the one to build, or type a steer.

options.label: Factory Floor
options.thesis: The whole marketplace as a production floor: every order a numbered lot, every claim a stamped inspection.
options.viewport: A full-bleed order board: ruled lots, mono numerals, a dispatch ticker, an amber flash-sale countdown stamped QC-PASS.
options.case: The roll's assignment. Every trust claim becomes a stamped inspection — fit, delivery, refund.
options.risk: Industrial-cold if the stamps and forms don't carry the confidence moment.

options.label: Ticker Floor
options.thesis: The market as a live price board: every product a listed lot, every deal a tick.
options.viewport: A scrolling deal ticker up top, a green/red price ladder as the catalog, flash sales as closing auctions.
options.case: Money-language the audience already trusts; delivery becomes a settlement time.
options.risk: Reads like an exchange, not a shop — buying must stay the obvious move.

options.label: Money Terminal
options.thesis: The checkout as a money terminal — the trust the audience already holds in their hands daily.
options.viewport: Product rows as a transaction list; checkout as a PIN-pad flow that ends in a printed receipt.
options.case: Familiar surface, next-generation form; the daily money ritual becomes the store.
options.risk: Too familiar — must feel like a system, not an app clone.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The catalog as a broadcast index: pages, not sections; prices as cyan figures on a fixed 40×24 grid.
options.viewport: A page-address header, numbered product pages, a cyan flash-sale countdown, REVEAL for return-policy detail.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: catalog pages, subpage carousels, REVEAL for fine print — but reads vintage.
options.risk: Retro nostalgia where the brief says extreme-modern; product photos fight a bitmap grid.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Products as glyphs on foundry paper: one axis slider morphs the whole catalog grid.
options.viewport: A single giant product wordmark; a weight slider drives the entire grid of cards beneath it.
options.case: Strong typographic hierarchy, but the white-paper register drifts toward the incumbent's quiet luxury.
options.risk: Feels like a type foundry showcase, not a place to buy.

options.label: Command Center
options.thesis: Flash sales as seven-segment countdowns; seller and admin dashboards as command consoles.
options.viewport: A black wall with a monumental seven-segment countdown, framed status blocks, hazard bands at the edges.
options.case: Countdown and console grammar fuses with flash sales and dashboards, but crisis chrome fights trust-first calm.
options.risk: Overstimulating — urgency must stay event-driven, never constant.

options.label: Cricket Scoreboard
options.thesis: The storefront as a live scorecard: every offer an over, every order an innings.
options.viewport: A persistent score strip of live deals; product rows as innings cards with running tallies.
options.case: A national screen ritual everyone reads instantly; urgency maps to powerplays.
options.risk: Sporty energy may undercut trust for sellers and payments.

options.label: Metro Signage
options.thesis: The storefront as a station network: categories are lines, products are stops on the board.
options.viewport: A line-diagram category rail; product listings styled as a departure board with clear routes.
options.case: Modern public infrastructure the city is proud of; navigation becomes wayfinding.
options.risk: The transit metaphor can obscure the commercial task.

options.label: Courier Sort
options.thesis: Delivery is the product: every order a tracked waybill moving down the sort line.
options.viewport: A sort-line of order cards, barcode ribbons, and a live tracking manifest beneath each product.
options.case: Makes the delivery promise physically legible — the marketplace's core proof.
options.risk: Density can read administrative, not inviting.

options.label: Load-Shed Board
options.lineage: utility schedule boards and public notice grids
options.thesis: Availability made legible like a power grid: honest schedules, posted windows, stamped statuses.
options.viewport: A stamped schedule grid: stock, delivery, and payout windows posted like utility notices.
options.case: Public-information honesty the whole country reads; trust through posted schedules.
options.risk: Outage associations may read negative for a trust-first brand.

options.label: ATM Terminal
options.thesis: Self-service banking for the whole store: every step a secure terminal, every action audited.
options.viewport: A function-key column, an LCD panel of products, checkout as a receipt-strip transaction.
options.case: Bank-grade trust vocabulary; balances, limits, and confirmations feel settled.
options.risk: Cold and institutional — the market's warmth must come through copy and motion.

options.label: Blueprint
options.thesis: The marketplace as a dimensioned spec: nothing unverified, every claim drawn to scale.
options.viewport: A title-block masthead, dimensioned product cards, section-marked category zones.
options.case: Structure made literal: verified dimensions, callouts, and revision history as trust cues.
options.risk: Schematic coldness — photography must stay desirable inside the frames.

options.label: CLI Terminal
options.thesis: The store as a fast terminal: every action a typed, confirmed command.
options.viewport: A prompt bar, product lines like ls output, checkout as a confirm prompt with a history.
options.case: Extreme structure and speed; power users feel it instantly.
options.risk: Too technical for the mobile majority — needs a gentle mode that keeps the grammar.

options.label: Control Room
options.thesis: The marketplace as an aired operation: every state metered, every chart a live waveform.
options.viewport: Metered status bars, scope-trace charts on dashboards, channel-strip navigation on the storefront.
options.case: Operation-level visibility for sellers; live meters make stock and delivery states physical.
options.risk: Machinery can obscure the simple act of buying.

options.label: SKU Scanner
options.thesis: SKU-level certainty: scan is search, cart, and verify in one laser line.
options.viewport: A scanning lane of product cards, laser-line hover states, beep-confirmed adds to cart.
options.case: Exactness as the brand: every product addressable, every price machine-read.
options.risk: Reads as warehouse ops unless the front feels like a shop.

options.label: Scaffold Frame
options.thesis: The marketplace as a building under honest construction: every load-bearing member visible.
options.viewport: A scaffold-grid catalog, a safety-banded flash sale, a 'built to spec' trust bar across the top.
options.case: Extreme structure with visible engineering; progress and statuses read like a site board.
options.risk: Rough texture may fight product photography — content zones need restraint.
